name: StorageFix
subtitle: Clean junk. Review your files.
promotionalText: One click to scan your Mac: caches, developer junk, old installers and leftovers of deleted apps. Review everything, then clean. Free, local, no ads.
description:
Make room with a clearer picture of your Mac.

Click Scan My Mac, allow your Home folder once, and StorageFix finds what is safe to clean: caches, developer junk, old installers and leftovers of apps you deleted. Review every item, then clean. Scans only read file information; nothing is removed until you confirm.

ONE-CLICK CLEANUP
Known, rebuildable caches: Xcode DerivedData, simulator and preview caches, Swift, npm, Gradle, Cargo and Bun package caches, browser and app caches, Adobe media cache and logs. Recommended categories are preselected. Caches are deleted permanently, apps rebuild them as needed, and the freed space is measured. Apple system caches are skipped and nothing is cleaned while its app is running.

OLD INSTALLERS AND APP LEFTOVERS
Finds disk images and installers in Downloads you no longer need, and settings and data left behind by apps you have deleted. Every item is listed before you confirm, and these go to the Trash so you can put them back.

FOR DEVELOPERS AND AI TINKERERS
Optional categories for Maven and CocoaPods repositories, Xcode Archives and local AI models from Ollama, Hugging Face and LM Studio, each with a clear warning and never preselected.

A GUIDED REVIEW
Follow five steps: choose a folder, understand the results, inspect candidates, confirm your review queue and verify the outcome with a fresh scan.

EXPLORE YOUR STORAGE
Switch between a treemap, ring and two-level sunburst linked to a ranked list. Drill into folders, follow breadcrumbs, search, sort and use Quick Look. Coverage details separate logical sizes, allocated sizes where macOS reports them, shared hard links, cloud placeholders and anything that could not be read.

COMPARE DUPLICATE COPIES
Duplicate comparison is optional and checks complete file contents. Preview copies, choose which one to keep and pick extra copies yourself. Suggestions never select files.

SIMILAR PHOTOS
Finds burst shots, edits and resized copies with Apple's on-device image analysis. The sharpest shot is marked Best; you pick what goes to the Trash, and every group keeps at least one photo.

FREE SPACE IN THE MENU BAR
See free space at a glance and start a scan from the menu bar. Hide it anytime.

FIND LARGE AND OLD FILES
Filter by size, type, name, path and last-modified date. Selections stay explicit when filters change.

ONE REVIEW QUEUE
Files from the map, file list and duplicates gather in one queue. The kept copy of a duplicate set is protected, every file is checked again just before it moves, and each result is reported individually. Files go to Finder Trash, where you can put them back.

HONEST OUTCOMES
After an operation, StorageFix shows the volume's measured free space before and after and lets you measure again. Space normally returns only when you empty Trash yourself. Export outcome reports as text, JSON or CSV; paths are left out unless you include them.

COMPARE SCANS OVER TIME
Use a scan as a baseline, optionally save it, rescan later and see which files appeared, disappeared or changed size.

LOCAL BY DESIGN
No account, advertising, tracking, analytics or file uploads. Scan data stays on your Mac. StorageFix remembers your Home folder permission so it asks only once; choose Forget Cache Access to remove it. Other folder access lasts for the session.

Also includes a read-only application inventory and a personal checklist linking to macOS settings. The checklist does not inspect security configuration or detect malware.

Requires macOS 14 or later. This edition does not uninstall applications. Reviewed files, installers and app leftovers go to Trash; only selected cache contents are deleted permanently.
whatsNew: Similar Photos finds burst shots and edited copies on-device. A free-space indicator in the menu bar. Scan My Mac with one Allow click, plus cleanup for developer caches, AI models, old installers and deleted-app leftovers.
